title: LingBot-World 2.0: An Agent-Piloted Infinite World Model
hook: Interactive world models usually run out of road — quality degrades, or the action set stays thin. LingBot-World 2.0 stays coherent forever and puts an agent inside to invent what's next.
key_points: Generates an unbounded interactive video world in real time, holding output quality steady via a causal pretraining paradigm.
Distills a real-time variant fast enough to stream 720p video at 60fps.
Expands the action/event vocabulary over prior LingBot-World: attacking, archery, spell-casting, shooting, plus richer text-driven events.
Pioneers an agentic harness inside the world model: a pilot agent runs characters, a director agent invents new environment content live.
Ships a 14B primary model plus a lightweight 1.3B variant, with a shared-session interface for multiple simultaneous players.
content_html: Interactive video world models tend to run out of road: either quality drifts the longer you play, or the world only supports a handful of scripted actions. LingBot-World 2.0 — also called LingBot-World-Infinity — pushes on both limits, and adds something new: an agent living inside the world it generates.
extra_html: Four upgrades define this version. A causal pretraining paradigm lets the model run an unbounded interaction horizon while holding output quality steady, rather than degrading session over session. A distilled real-time variant streams 720p video at 60fps, fast enough to feel live. The action and event vocabulary grows substantially — attacking, archery, spell-casting, shooting, and a richer set of text-driven events beyond the original LingBot-World. And most notably, the team builds an agentic harness directly into the world model: a pilot agent plans and executes character behavior, while a separate director agent synthesizes new environmental content as the scene plays out — the world authors itself while someone (or something) is inside it. The team pairs a 14B primary model with a lightweight 1.3B counterpart for single-GPU deployment, and adds an interface so multiple players can share the same generated world simultaneously. Zelin Gao and colleagues, arXiv 2026 (21 HF community upvotes).

related.title: LingBot-Video: A Sparse-MoE Video Diffusion World Model
related.hook: Video diffusion models are usually dense — every parameter fires on every frame. LingBot-Video swaps in a sparse Mixture-of-Experts, then grades its own physics with a VLM judge.

related.title: World Models Lack a Persistent State
related.hook: Today's video world models render great frames but treat the world like a tracking shot: look away and back, and off-screen events freeze instead of running on — the moon keeps orbiting unwatched.

related.title: MIRA: A Multiplayer World Model for Rocket League
related.hook: Single-player world models treat other agents as scenery. This one, trained on 10,000 hours of Rocket League, tracks four players' independent actions at once — and stays coherent for hours.

related.title: AlayaWorld: An Open-Source Framework for Playable Video Worlds
related.hook: Building a game world the old way means authoring every asset by hand. AlayaWorld generates it live instead — combat, spell-casting, monster summoning — and open-sources the whole pipeline.

flashcards.prompt: What's new about how LingBot-World 2.0 uses agents, compared to a typical interactive world model?
flashcards.back_html: It runs an agentic harness inside the world model: a pilot agent plans and executes character behavior, while a director agent invents new environmental content as the scene unfolds.

flashcards.prompt: What lets LingBot-World 2.0 sustain an unbounded interaction horizon without degrading?

choices.text: A causal pretraining paradigm designed specifically to keep output quality consistent over an unbounded horizon
It caps every session at a fixed short length to avoid degradation
It re-renders the entire world from scratch every few seconds
It relies on a human operator to manually patch quality drops

flashcards.explanation_html: The unbounded, consistent-quality horizon comes from a dedicated causal pretraining paradigm — a separate step from the real-time distillation that enables 60fps/720p streaming.

flashcards.prompt: How does LingBot-World 2.0 achieve real-time 720p video at 60fps?
flashcards.back_html: By distilling a dedicated real-time variant from the base model — a separate step from the causal pretraining that handles the unbounded horizon.
